topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Temporal Locality
explanation: Temporal locality is a principle of locality of reference asserting that recently accessed data or instructions are highly likely to be accessed again in the near future. Caching strategies exploit this by retaining recently used cache lines in the faster, upper levels of the memory hierarchy (L1, L2). When the CPU requires data, the high probability of a cache hit avoids a costly main memory access. This retention mechanism minimizes memory access latency and maximizes the effective memory bandwidth, crucial for performance in iterative loops and stack operations.
